clues: It hosts the Wife Carrying World Championships.
Nokia started here in 1865, as a pulp mill on a set of rapids.
It has been named the happiest country in the world nine years in a row.
Its capital is Helsinki.
fact: The sport of wife carrying began in Sonkajärvi in 1992 and became a world championship in 1996. The country also has over 180,000 recorded lakes.

clues: Over 90% of its wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.
It grows about 42% of the world’s vanilla.
Lemurs live naturally here and nowhere else.
It’s the world’s fourth-largest island, off the south-east coast of Africa.
fact: Millions of years of isolation let its plants and animals evolve on their own. In 2023 it produced 42% of the world’s vanilla.

clues: It has the world’s largest area of freshwater lakes.
It has the longest coastline of any country.
It shares the longest international land border in the world.
It’s the second-largest country by area, and its capital is Ottawa.
fact: Its lakes are why it ranks only fourth by land area despite being second by total area. Its border with its southern neighbour is the longest land border on Earth.

clues: A temple-building company here traces its roots back to the year 578.
It is made up of 14,125 islands.
Its highest mountain is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.
Its capital is Tokyo.
fact: Kongō Gumi, founded in 578 in Osaka, built and repaired shrines and temples for more than 1,400 years. Mount Fuji, 3,776 m, became a World Heritage Site in 2013.

clues: The Nazca culture flourished on its coast.
The largest empire in the pre-Columbian Americas ruled from a city here.
Machu Picchu is here.
Its capital is Lima.
fact: The Inca built the largest empire in the pre-Columbian Americas, with Cusco as its capital. Machu Picchu is the citadel that became its icon.

clues: It lifted its ban on television and the internet only in 1999.
Its national anthem is called “The Thunder Dragon Kingdom”.
About 71% of it is forest, and it famously measures Gross National Happiness.
It’s a Himalayan kingdom between China and India. Its capital is Thimphu.
fact: It was one of the last countries in the world to introduce television. Its name in its own language means “Land of the Thunder Dragon”.

clues: In 1932 its army fought a “war” against emus, and abandoned it.
It has the longest fence in the world: 5,614 km, built to keep dingoes out.
The world’s largest coral reef system, over 2,300 km long, lies off its coast.
Its capital is Canberra.
fact: Soldiers with machine guns spent five weeks in the Emu War in 1932. The emus scattered into small groups and the cull was called off.

clues: Officially it has no capital at all, just a “federal city”.
It has four language regions: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
It’s the birthplace of the Red Cross.
It has been neutral since the 16th century, and hasn’t fought an international war since 1815.
fact: Bern is the seat of government but not, legally, the capital. Its neutrality was recognised by Europe’s powers in 1648.

clues: It ranks first among the world’s 17 “megadiverse” countries.
It borders every other country on its continent except Ecuador and Chile.
It has the largest Portuguese-speaking population in the world.
It’s the fifth-largest country on Earth by area.
fact: It borders nine countries and one French territory: every neighbour on its continent except Ecuador and Chile. It’s also the world’s fifth-largest country.

clues: Along with Liberia, it’s the only African country never fully colonised.
It hosts the headquarters of the African Union Commission.
It’s the second most populous country in Africa, and has no coastline.
Its capital is Addis Ababa.
fact: Italy occupied it from 1936 to 1941 but never secured the whole country. Around 138 million people live there.

clues: It’s the most sparsely populated sovereign state in the world.
About 30% of its people are nomadic or semi-nomadic.
Its capital is the coldest capital city in the world.
Genghis Khan founded an empire here in 1206. It’s landlocked between Russia and China.
fact: Ulaanbaatar averages −1.3 °C over the year, colder than any other capital.

clues: Bats were its only known native land mammals until a fossil find in 2006.
In 1893 it became the first nation to give all women the vote.
Its national icon is a flightless bird.
Its capital is Wellington.
fact: With no mammal predators, several of its birds evolved to lose the power of flight, including the kiwi.

clues: It’s the only NATO member with no standing army.
The English word “geyser” comes from a hot spring here.
Its parliament, the Althing, dates back to around 930.
About 35% of its roughly 395,000 people live in its capital, Reykjavík.
fact: Geysir is the oldest known geyser in the world. Its parliament has a claim to being one of the longest-running in the world.

clues: More than half its people live on one island, the most heavily populated island on Earth.
It’s the world’s largest archipelagic state, with between 13,000 and 17,000 islands.
It has the largest Muslim population of any country.
Its capital is Jakarta.
fact: Java holds more than half of its people. Islam is followed by about 87% of the population.

clues: It claims about 1.25 million km² of Antarctica.
Easter Island has belonged to it since 1888.
Its Atacama Desert was the site of the 2010 San José mine collapse.
Its capital is Santiago.
fact: It also administers the Juan Fernández Islands in the Pacific. Its Antarctic claim is called the Chilean Antarctic Territory.
